Found 11 reproducible issues:

1. **[P1] `--dry-run` executes `shell()` commands.** [function.rs:548](/work/crate/src/function.rs:548) calls `run_command` without checking `dry_run`. A justfile containing `x := shell('touch marker')` creates `marker` during `just --dry-run main`. Backticks correctly suppress execution. This can run destructive commands during an expected preview.

2. **[P1] The default chooser permits shell injection through the justfile path.** [subcommand.rs:243](/work/crate/src/subcommand.rs:243) interpolates the path into shell source without escaping it. Running `just --choose` from a directory named `chooser'; touch INJECTED; #` created `INJECTED`, even with `fzf` absent. Both the outer chooser command and nested preview need proper quoting.

3. **[P2] Caching parsed files by path mixes up module identities and overrides.** [compiler.rs:19](/work/crate/src/compiler.rs:19) reuses an AST containing context-specific module paths and variable numbers. With `mod a 'common.just'` and `mod b 'common.just'`, invoking both modules’ recipes prints module path `b` only once. Separately, when two modules import the same variable declaration, overriding `a::x=first b::x=second` makes both modules see `second`.

4. **[P2] Parent bindings can shadow unevaluated local assignments.** [evaluator.rs:411](/work/crate/src/evaluator.rs:411) searches the parent scope before resolving local assignments. For `A := HEX` followed by `HEX := 'custom'`, `--evaluate` gives `A` the built-in hexadecimal alphabet instead of `custom`. The same problem occurs when a submodule redeclares a parent variable, making results depend on evaluation order.

5. **[P2] `--fmt` removes module privacy.** [item.rs:59](/work/crate/src/item.rs:59) ignores the module’s `private` field when formatting. Formatting `[private]` followed by `mod hidden` removes the attribute; afterward, the previously hidden module appears in `--list`.

6. **[P2] Formatting multiline module documentation produces invalid source.** [item.rs:67](/work/crate/src/item.rs:67) writes cooked documentation behind a single comment prefix. `[doc("first\nsecond")]` becomes `# first` followed by bare `second`. `--fmt` succeeds, but the resulting justfile fails to parse. Preserve the attribute or correctly encode every documentation line.

7. **[P2] Lazy dependency scanning takes exponential time on shared dependency graphs.** [justfile.rs:196](/work/crate/src/justfile.rs:196) traverses every dependency path without tracking visited recipes. A 44-recipe graph where each recipe depends on the preceding two exceeded a three-second timeout in the release build; the identical graph without `set lazy` completed in approximately two milliseconds.

8. **[P2] `--no-deps` still evaluates variables used only by skipped dependencies.** [justfile.rs:198](/work/crate/src/justfile.rs:198) includes dependencies when collecting lazy variable references regardless of `config.no_dependencies`. With `set lazy`, a dependency-only variable defined as `error('dependency only')` makes `just --no-deps main` fail before running `main`.

9. **[P2] Long operator chains bypass the parser’s recursion limit and abort.** [parser.rs:717](/work/crate/src/parser.rs:717) recursively calls `parse_conjunct` without increasing the guarded recursion depth. An assignment concatenating 10,000 empty strings terminates the release binary with a stack-overflow abort instead of a diagnostic. Slash chains have the same unguarded recursion.

10. **[P2] `--quiet` does not suppress script recipe output.** [recipe.rs:540](/work/crate/src/recipe.rs:540) launches scripts without redirecting stdout and stderr for quiet mode. Both shebang recipes and `[script('sh')]` recipes still print to both streams, contrary to the option’s “Suppress all output” contract and linewise recipe behavior.

11. **[P2, unstable feature] User-defined functions discard module evaluation state.** [evaluator.rs:226](/work/crate/src/evaluator.rs:226) creates a fresh root scope and empty override map. With `x := 'original'` and `f() := x`, invoking `x=override` makes direct access return `override` while `f()` returns `original`. Function parameters also leak into evaluation of module assignments: `x := 'global'; y := x; f(x) := y` makes `f('argument')` return `argument`.
